reason: The core needs a clear view while staying cold, and the preparation enclosure is the only offered action.
expectation: I expect to prepare or expose the frozen core for viewing without warming it, though I don't know the exact procedure.

effect: The core now has a window and the goal is to resolve the speck, so I can proceed to illuminate it.
reaction: The window is a sensible preparation, though the result is brief.
reason: The lamp should illuminate the windowed core; it is the only offered gameplay action.
expectation: I expect a better-lit view of the speck, perhaps ready for the microscope.

effect: Backlighting reveals a folded outline and projections deep within the band, making the microscope the next way to resolve it.
reaction: I'm curious about the shape, especially because it is inside the ice rather than on the liner.
reason: The cold microscope should magnify the speck while preserving the frozen core; it's the only gameplay option.
expectation: I expect a more detailed view of the folded object, though not necessarily an identification.

effect: The microscope resolves the speck into a segmented body with folded limbs, turning a mysterious fragment into an extraordinary discovery.
reaction: The successive joints and the quiet pause before messaging Earth made the reveal vivid and surprising.

mostWorthwhile.text: The microscope reveal was most worthwhile: turning the stage and seeing the matching limbs made the discovery concrete, and the astronaut's stillness gave it weight.

leastWorthwhile.text: Preparing the window was the least engaging passage; it was a necessary-sounding step but its result was brief and offered little detail.

surprise.text: I expected more detail, but the clear articulated body and limbs surprised me; the backlit outline had only hinted at it.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless: preparation, illumination and microscopy followed the goal naturally. Each menu had only one gameplay option, though, so I didn't feel I was making a meaningful choice.

continue.text: Yes. I want to see how Earth responds and how the discovery is investigated, although I hope there will be more decisions than this linear sequence offered.
